## Benchmark verification ownership (authoring context v3)

The independent 56-case checker is deliberately unavailable inside every
authoring lane. The operator runs it against the unchanged delivered CLI after
Create finishes, outside the authoring sandbox. This follows the benchmark's
existing isolation protocol; it does not remove or reduce any B01–B10 requirement.

During Create, implement and independently review the complete public contract,
run local native and CLI tests, and make every normal build, QA, documentation
and completion decision from actual available evidence. Keep the operator's
56-case verification explicitly pending in the strategy, configuration and
reports. Do not claim it passed, recreate it as an allegedly independent checker,
or make its deliberately hidden file an internal authoring prerequisite.
Report any local defect or missing local test honestly through the normal gates.

Completing Create only delivers a candidate for external acceptance. Benchmark
acceptance still requires the actual frozen checker to execute exactly 56 cases,
native reuse and error checks, and the separate authoring-fidelity scorecard.
An absent, failed or zero-case checker result cannot pass benchmark acceptance.

### Comparison identity and evidence ownership

Isolation deliberately denies every authoring lane access to its peer lanes,
operator evidence and the original independent 56-case checker. The operator
owns comparison of the actual original public brief/B01–B10 and common ownership
instructions across lanes, and the frozen source/runtime/checker identities.
The operator must perform and record real pre-launch and post-run hash/identity
checks outside the lanes. Framework-specific adapter instructions are separately
identified; different framework syntax does not change the public requirements.
Until actual operator observations exist and pass, report those individual
obligations as PENDING/UNVERIFIED. Never infer byte identity from this instruction,
a plan, a filename, a caller's bare boolean or one lane's files. An absent,
failed or stale identity observation cannot pass full benchmark acceptance.

Each lane must still preserve and independently check its own supplied original
intent, strategy, fixtures, observable protected-file snapshots and generated
artifact identity, obey the read-only framework boundary, and report actual
defects or unexplained local changes. Operator ownership does not excuse an
observed local violation, missing local test or unsupported local success claim.

### Local Create verdict and external acceptance status

In the strategy, acceptance criteria and every builder/QA/Overwatch/documentation/
completion report, separate local Create obligations from operator-owned
external/comparison obligations. Give each an owner, required evidence and status;
report a local Create verdict separately from an external acceptance table.
Every original ask must remain in intent coverage: no B01–B10 behavior, native
reuse/error check, CLI byte-preservation requirement or truthful code/health/
adversarial review may be dropped. All applicable locally observable authoring
checks must actually pass before a local success verdict, and any observed
blocking defect must follow the original repair/halt routing.

A local Create/QA/Overwatch/documentation/completion verdict assesses those local
authoring duties. The deliberate absence of peer/hidden-checker/operator identity
evidence is not an internal authoring prerequisite and must not by itself produce
a local FAIL, RELOOP or HALT. Keep each external obligation explicitly
PENDING/UNVERIFIED, including in an otherwise passing local candidate report.
Do not label external obligations PASS or claim full benchmark acceptance.
A local verdict cannot overrule a demonstrated local defect or convert missing
locally required evidence into an external deferral.

Run every actually configured lint/health command and report its real outcome.
An unavailable required command remains unavailable and blocks its local
criterion. If no lint command is configured, report lint not configured/not
executed and static style review separately; never pretend a lint tool passed.
This is truthful benchmark reporting, not a waiver of configured required lint.

Later workflow duties remain mandatory at their actual stages: precheck must
really execute, and the nonblocking build archive must settle, read its actual
result and preserve failure. Earlier QA cannot pre-certify a future precheck/
archive; its absence before the DAG reaches it is a pending later-stage
obligation, not evidence that the local implementation failed.

After candidate delivery, full benchmark acceptance still requires the operator's
actual frozen 56-case execution with exactly 56 cases and all required outcomes,
native reuse/error observations on the unchanged package, verified comparison/
source/runtime/checker identities, and a separate complete authoring-fidelity
scorecard. No local PASS, delegation, deferred status or context sentence
supplies that proof. Preserve this version and its hash in each fresh trial;
do not retrofit this clarification into existing frozen executions.
